purpose: Connect the first-frame/reopen signature to exact installed-driver completion gates, rather than repeat passing echo captures.
queries: site.learn.microsoft.com USB cancelled transfer partial bytes TransferBufferLength
site.learn.microsoft.com URB canceled bulk IN transfer data length STATUS_CANCELLED
site.github.com/quic/eud COM reset USB data toggle
site.learn.microsoft.com USB reset pipe clear stall data toggle pending transfers

sources.finding: Returned TransferBufferLength describes transferred bytes; short-packet semantics depend on transfer flags. This does not establish validity of every positive length on every failure/cancellation.
sources.use: Require status/actual transfer evidence alongside length in the proposed capture. No blanket partial-on-error assumption.

sources.finding: Both illustrated completion paths branch on failure before accumulating transferred bytes.
sources.limit: KMDF sample differs from the installed Qualcomm WDM driver; it does not prove a defect or provide an EUD patch.

sources.finding: Cancellation can coexist with partial data. This generic possibility was already used in RX49; the new finding is the exact logger/status gate in our installed driver.
Different reset/clear-stall URBs affect host/device toggle state differently. This is reused RX47/RX56 material, not a newly discovered mechanism.
sources.limit: RX56 maps the installed reset selector to 0x1e, so do not assume this path resets host DATA0/1. No physical PID measurement or new reset experiment.

sources.use: Supports interpreting completion status and coordinating cancellation/recovery. The proposed observation does not introduce another reset or re-enumeration experiment.

result: No ready EUD-specific COM fix found by these focused queries. No outside person contacted. First-frame association and precise status gates are new measured/static evidence; failure-time joint capture is still required.
